header.name: forum
header.tagline: Route a request, run it in waves, keep a record you can re-check.

flows.title: How a plain request becomes an answer with a record behind it
flows.alt: Eight stages from a routed request to a hash-chained record: route, context, plan, dispatch, verdict, escalate, synthesize, ledger. A result that fails its verdict sends the task up a ladder of stronger models and is graded again. Re-checking the record reports the chain and the payloads separately, and a payload that was never stored is skipped rather than counted as held.
flows.footnote: Re-checking a run reads the record. It does not re-run the models that produced it.

stages.title: Route
stages.note: A roster picks the lane, and no model is called to do it.

stages.title: Context
stages.note: What shaped the plan is written down before the plan is.

stages.title: Plan
stages.note: A dependency graph, resolved into waves that run at once.

stages.title: Dispatch
stages.note: Waves run across whichever executors the run was given.

stages.title: Verdict
stages.note: A judge grades each result, and the grade is recorded.

stages.title: Escalate
stages.note: A failed grade sends the task up a ladder of models.

stages.title: Synthesize
stages.note: One answer, held to the contract the route selected.

stages.title: Ledger
stages.note: Each step above already sits in a hash-chained log.

cards.kicker: no model runs, and nothing goes missing quietly
cards.title: What happens to a piece of context when the budget is tight
cards.alt: Seven things that can happen to one piece of context on its way to a task, and why each one lands that way. Text under its cap is kept whole, text over it is trimmed to the cap and measured again from what survived, and when two caps bind equally the reason names the total so a reader can tell the run is nearly out. Empty text is still recorded as a check. A character sitting on the cut is dropped rather than mangled, because the trim is measured in bytes. The marked row is the one where a piece is dropped whole, and even then the record keeps a row for it.
cards.footnote: Four numbers ride with every row: bytes and tokens on arrival, bytes and tokens admitted. Tokens are approximate, UTF-8 bytes over four rounded up, so a cap is a guardrail rather than a measurement. forum context preflight runs the same arithmetic before a model call is spent, and the run record carries the tally.

fields.note: Neither the source cap nor the total is set, so nothing binds and the text still gets a row.
A run that trimmed nothing says so, which is what makes a quiet run readable later.
What was admitted is measured again from what survived, rather than assumed from the cap.
On a tie the reason names the total, so it reads as a run running out and not one large input.
A cap at or below zero drops the text whole. The record still carries the piece that went.
Zero tokens costs nothing and still counts, so the tally matches the work done.
The trim counts bytes, so a half character decodes away before a task sees it.
